title: Cauliflower Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Cauliflower Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Cauliflower nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and boron in koliplor, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Cauliflower nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your koliplor (cauliflower) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, boron, molybdenum, calcium, potassium, phosphorus, magnesium and sulfur. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Cauliflower plants whose older leaves turn pale and reddish purple from nitrogen shortage
heroImage.credit: Rasbak (Wikimedia Commons user), CC BY SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, molybdenum, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But boron, calcium and sulfur stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which cauliflower nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Cauliflower nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

blocks.text: Shows first on the young leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of koliplor

Brown or pink patches on the curd and a hollow, water soaked stem.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a cauliflower nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest cauliflower nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in cauliflower

blocks.alt: Cauliflower plants whose older leaves turn pale and reddish purple from nitrogen shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Rasbak (Wikimedia Commons user), CC BY SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text: Older leaves turn yellow and get red color starting at the edges, then die or drop. Growth is stunted and roots are weak. A shortage of nitrogen on young plants is one cause of buttoning, where tiny curds form early and the plant stops growing leaves. You see it most at this stage: from transplanting to curd formation.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in koliplor
Sandy or light soils, heavy rain or irrigation, low organic matter, raw straw or manure. Too little nitrogen early in the season.
How to tell it apart

Phosphorus shortage also reddens leaves, but phosphorus leaves are dull bluish green while nitrogen leaves are light green. Buttoning also comes from overaged seedlings or heat. To be sure, soil test and leaf tissue test. Note whether the old leaves yellow first.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate based on the soil test. For a quick green up, KAU suggests a urea spray at 10 grams per liter of water every 15 days.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, give enough nitrogen and water for fast leaf growth in the first weeks after transplanting, and use young, healthy seedlings.
Boron deficiency in cauliflower

After the curd forms, water soaked areas appear on the stem and curd. The stem becomes hollow, with water soaked tissue inside that later turns brown or black. Brown or pink patches form on the curd surface (brown rot or browning), and the curd tastes bitter. Young leaves stay small, stiff and light green with reddish or brown edges, and in severe cases the growing point dies. You see it most at this stage: curd formation and development.
Why boron deficiency happens in koliplor
High soil pH and alkaline or overlimed soils, sandy soils where boron leaches, low organic matter, high nitrogen or calcium. Dry or cold wet spells.
How to tell it apart
Hollow stem from fast growth or too much nitrogen stays bright inside. Boron hollow stem browns. To be sure, cut stems to check for brown cavities. Soil test and leaf tissue test for boron.
What to apply for boron deficiency

The National Horticulture Board of India suggests borax at 10 to 15 kg per hectare in acid soils, more in neutral or alkaline soils. KAU gives a borax spray at 1 gram per liter of water. Delaware extension advises about 3 pounds of boron per acre before planting, or a spray of 1.0 to 1.5 pounds of Solubor per acre before heading if none went in the soil. Do not mix borax with calcium or ammonium fertilizer.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add boron in the basal fertilizer for every cauliflower crop on light soils, and treat the nursery too.
Molybdenum deficiency in cauliflower

Young leaves yellow at the edges, and the leaf blade fails to grow, in bad cases leaving only the midrib (whiptail). Leaves are thick, distorted and cupped. The growing point is deformed, so the curd does not develop, or late shortage gives loose curds with small leaves pushing through. Affected plants often come in patches. You see it most at this stage: seedling and young plant stage, and at curd formation if it comes late.
Why molybdenum deficiency happens in koliplor
Acid soils, mostly below pH 5.5, where molybdenum is locked up. Low organic matter makes it worse.
How to tell it apart

Boron shortage also deforms young plants, so check both. Nitrogen shortage yellows old leaves but does not make strap leaves. To be sure, soil pH test and a leaf tissue test. A trial spray of sodium molybdate on a few plants should bring normal new growth.
What to apply for molybdenum deficiency

NSW DPI suggests about 50 grams of sodium molybdate in 100 liters of water sprayed on the leaves, or 150 ml of that mix at the base of each plant. For the next crop, mix about 1 kg sodium molybdate per hectare with the fertilizer, or water the seedbed with 40 grams in 50 liters per 10 square meters one to two weeks before transplanting. KAU gives a 1 gram per liter foliar spray. Lime acid soils.

Sold here with molybdenum: **Tierramino Molybdenum** by Unilox Far East Resources Inc. (16 percent molybdenum), **YaraVita Teprosyn Mo** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (15 percent P2O5 and 15.3 percent molybdenum), **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate General Purpose** by Sagrex Corporation (2 percent Fe, 0.5 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 3 percent S with Cu, Zn, B, Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [molybdenum deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/molybdenum-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils to about pH 6 well before planting, and add molybdenum to the nursery.
Calcium deficiency in cauliflower

Dead lesions form on the tips and edges of young leaves and spread inward with a yellow border (tip burn). The youngest leaves become claw shaped, cupped and brittle, and the leaf edges can look glassy. Curd segments can turn brown and glassy and parts of the curd die. You see it most at this stage: rapid leaf growth and curd development.
Why calcium deficiency happens in koliplor
Restricted calcium uptake rather than low soil calcium: water stress (dry or waterlogged), high ammonium, potassium, magnesium or sodium, and acid sandy soils. Low boron also limits calcium use.
How to tell it apart

Boron shortage also damages the growing point but gives hollow stems and brown curds. Downy mildew and black rot are diseases with spots or V shaped lesions. To be sure, soil test for calcium, pH and boron.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

Keep soil moisture even. On acid soil, KAU suggests lime at about 250 kg per hectare when pH is 5.5 to 6, or about 840 kg per hectare in two doses when pH is 3.5 to 4.5. Gypsum on soil that is not acid. Check boron too.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime before planting, water evenly, and avoid heavy ammonium and potash.
Potassium deficiency in cauliflower

Leaf edges turn yellow, then light brown and later dark brown, and curl upward. Leaves lose their waxy coating. The dead tissue spreads from the edges toward the middle, and stems become weak. You see it most at this stage: curd formation.
Why potassium deficiency happens in koliplor
Acid or sandy soils, heavy rain or irrigation, drought, low potassium reserves, and soils rich in magnesium.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage yellows between the veins. Potassium shortage burns the edges first. To be sure, soil test for potassium and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply muriate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses. For an immediate remedy, KAU suggests a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water with a sticker. Keep soil pH above 6.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include potash in the basal fertilizer and side dressing.
Phosphorus deficiency in cauliflower

Older leaves turn a pale bluish green with purple color, especially along the veins, and the undersides often turn red. Plants are stunted with short, thin shoots, and vigour and yield drop. You see it most at this stage: seedling and early growth, in cold or wet soil.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in koliplor
Acid or calcareous soils, iron rich soils, low organic matter, cold or wet weather and weak roots.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage can also redden leaves, but those leaves stay light green, not bluish. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency
Apply phosphorus near the roots based on the soil test. KAU lists single superphosphate for a quick correction and rock phosphate or bone meal for the long term, with best uptake near pH 6.2 to 7.0.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use a phosphorus starter at transplanting.
Magnesium deficiency in cauliflower

Older leaves yellow between the veins, starting at the edges and moving toward the midrib, while the veins stay green. In severe cases dead spots form between the veins, and old leaves become stiff and drop early. You see it most at this stage: curd formation.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in koliplor
Sandy or acid soils, soils rich in potassium, heavy potash fertilizer, and cold wet periods. Cauliflower is one of the crucifers most prone to it.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage yellows the whole leaf, veins included. To be sure, soil test for magnesium and potassium, and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

KAU suggests magnesium sulfate in a band near the plants at about 80 kg per hectare (32 kg per acre). A foliar spray of magnesium sulfate gives faster relief. Do not apply magnesium and potassium together.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use dolomitic lime on acid soils.
Sulfur deficiency in cauliflower

Yellowing starts in the young leaves and moves to older ones. Leaves turn uniformly light green or yellow and feel stiff, may show red color, and later curl inward. Often only thin leaf stalks form, and in severe cases seedlings die. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in koliplor
Acid or sandy soils where sulfate leaches, low organic matter, waterlogged soils, and no sulfur in the fertilizer.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage starts on old leaves. To be sure, soil test for sulfate and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for sulfur deficiency
Use ammonium sulfate as part of the nitrogen. KAU suggests sulfur dust at about 25 kg per hectare (10 kg per acre) on sulfur deficient soil, and gypsum on alkaline soil.

Sold here with sulfur: **Farmfix Sulfur** by Philippine FarmFix, Inc. (99 percent sulfur), **VSI Sulfur Powder** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (99.5 percent sulfur), **Atlas Ammosul** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur) and **Philphos 21 0 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 (ammonium sulfate)). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give some sulfur every crop.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any cauliflower nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your koliplor needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Cauliflower nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my koliplor leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: older leaves yellow with red edges, and small button curds form too early. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at sulfur deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in cauliflower?
items.a: Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate based on the soil test. For a quick green up, KAU suggests a urea spray at 10 grams per liter of water every 15 days.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes boron deficiency in cauliflower?
items.a: The National Horticulture Board of India suggests borax at 10 to 15 kg per hectare in acid soils, more in neutral or alkaline soils. KAU gives a borax spray at 1 gram per liter of water.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes molybdenum deficiency in cauliflower?
items.a: NSW DPI suggests about 50 grams of sodium molybdate in 100 liters of water sprayed on the leaves, or 150 ml of that mix at the base of each plant. For the next crop, mix about 1 kg sodium molybdate per hectare with the fertilizer, or water the seedbed with 40 grams in 50 liters per 10 square meters one to two weeks before transplanting.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my koliplor lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the cauliflower nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
